name: pup-update-command-policy

provenance.q6_submit: 0xC0184401 family dispatcher 0x637770, sub0 -> worker 0x638230; argument block {u64 cpuaddr@0x00, u64 size@0x08, u32 mode@0x10, u32 pad@0x14}. The cpuaddr is read as the user address the SBL driver pins and maps (gpuvm.c `map` 0x61ae20 / extractCpuAddrUser -> vm_fault_quick_hold_pages -> gbase_map): it must be held to a 0x4000 boundary and one 0x4000 unit is mapped. The size is round checked to 0x4000 at 0x638295..0x6382b9 (EINVAL 0x16 otherwise), so only 1..0x4000 survives. The mode word is compared against 2 at 0x638376 (which adds a second engine pass); 0 requests the base transfer only. The pointer field is therefore 0 -- the earlier model ({op, ptr, length}, pointer at 8) named the SIZE field and replaced it with the staging address, which is exactly the deterministic EINVAL the live runs measured.
provenance.own1_trigger: 0xC0184404 Tag-4 sub3 0x637BFF, historical mid-fail geometry (4 x 0x4000, hole in the last segment); its block is {u16 mode@0x00, u64@0x08, u64@0x10} -- the semantics of the two u64 are NOT proven, so no size/mode constraint is declared for it
provenance.status_read: 0xC010440A gate [r12+8]==0x104; where the response lands is not proven, so the command declares no pointer field and a caller cannot fill its 260 byte response

notes: only these three commands may be invoked; the device path is fixed by policy
0xC0184402/0xC0184403 exist in the family but are not needed by the first experiment profile
the declared pointer field is the offset the provider overwrites with the address of its own staging region; the host value at that offset never reaches the device
the request size and the mode word are the caller's and are not touched by the provider: the driver validates them
